A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same regression–simulation–homotopy framework and camera-pose applications. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary materials support reliable comparison despite the revised title and layout.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic generalized PnP and GRPS experiments, LaMAR evaluations, and supplementary numerical-stability and noise-resilience results.

after.justification: V2 retains original synthetic and LaMAR results and reports additional initialization-ablation and Gröbner-basis comparison results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the network architectures and loss, correspondence simulation, and single-root continuation procedure remain unchanged. Random initialization is introduced as an experimental control, not a replacement for the proposed regression-based method.

E1.justification: Both retain synthetic generalized PnP and GRPS tasks and the CAB, HGE, and LIN sequences of LaMAR. V2 removes the synthetic RANSAC test at 50% outliers, retaining 10–40%. Rolling-shutter and inverse-kinematics applications are proposed only as future work.

E2.justification: The synthetic and LaMAR RANSAC evaluations change from reporting Simulator HC alone to direct comparisons with Gröbner Bases (Tables 2–4), substantially expanding practical baseline comparisons. Table 1 also adds a random-initialization control; 'Only Net' and 'LM' are retained under the clearer names 'Pred Initial' and 'Pred Initial + LM'.

E3.justification: Section 6.3 revises the hardware description from CPU evaluation/GPU training to CPU and GPU use for training and evaluation, without resolving allocation by method. V2 introduces the random-initialization control and specifies real-root filtering and parallel reprojection-based selection for the added Gröbner-basis RANSAC comparisons. Core sample counts and iteration limits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds an ablation testing the importance of predicted initialization: random initialization achieves 22% success versus 100% for predicted initialization. The outlier-robustness comparison gains a Gröbner-basis comparator but loses the 50% outlier case. Existing correspondence-count, numerical-stability, and noise-resilience analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both use 1000-trial summaries, error distributions, boxplots, and LaMAR medians. No new seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear. Explicit median labels in Figure 4b annotate an existing boxplot statistic rather than introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Multiple central results change. Table 1 replaces Simulator HC's rotation error/time of 0.137 degrees/0.160 ms with 0.032 degrees/0.316 ms. Table 3 replaces LaMAR success rates of 63/78/82% with 68/84/86%, adds baseline results, and removes inlier counts. Figure 4 revises speedup ratios, and new control results appear. These are reported revisions, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The homotopy derivations and geometric polynomial formulations remain unchanged. V2 clarifies parentheses in the standard rotation-error expression and replaces repeated metric formulas with a cross-reference; these do not establish a substantive change to theory, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The main framework and high-success, efficient-solver contributions remain. The conclusion narrows the GRPS speed claim from 'at least 20×' to 'around 17×' faster than polynomial elimination. The introduction additionally claims that learning a solution is easier than learning a problem-solution pair.

C2.justification: New ablation discussion argues that HC exploits approximate predicted initializations more effectively than LM. The RANSAC discussion explains the cost of selecting among roughly 46 real Gröbner-basis solutions. Supplementary Section 13 proposes untested rolling-shutter and inverse-kinematics applications; existing ambiguity and degeneracy qualifications remain.

D1.justification: V2 removes the detailed ray-noise construction and renormalization procedure, the parallel HC baseline's Cayley-parameter/27-root explanation, and precise outlier-generation details. It revises hardware-use documentation and adds Gröbner-basis solution-selection details. Omission of the baseline explanation does not establish that its implementation changed.

R1.justification: The introduction adds an argument that solution regression is easier than learning problem-solution pairs, sharpening its positioning against Hruby et al. The literature review otherwise remains stable. The additional Fischler–Bolles reference duplicates the already cited RANSAC work rather than adding a distinct prior work.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, affiliation, and some headings; edits the abstract and experimental discussion; corrects an Algorithm 1 cross-reference; and adds acknowledgments and supplementary discussion. The overall narrative order and most explanatory text remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 are restructured for initialization variants and paired baseline comparisons, and supplementary Table 4 is added. Figure 2's endpoint labels are corrected and Figure 4b gains median annotations. Figure 3, Algorithm 1, and supplementary plots are relocated; the original stability and noise plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The initialization control and direct Gröbner-basis comparisons strengthen evidence for the learned starting solution and practical RANSAC performance, addressing gaps in v1's evaluation. These gains are limited by removal of the 50% outlier case and useful implementation details, while substantial timing revisions and hardware allocation remain insufficiently explained. Overall, the evidential support improves modestly.
